population.span: In this double-blind, randomized study, hospitalized patients were randomly assigned to receive either a lactobacilli-fermented milk or a placebo on a daily basis.

endpoint.span: Among 89 randomized patients, antibiotic-associated diarrhea occurred

estimate.span: Among 89 randomized patients, antibiotic-associated diarrhea occurred in seven of 44 patients (15.9%) in the lactobacilli group and in 16 of 45 patients (35.6%) in the placebo group (OR 0.34, 95% CI 0.125 to 0.944; P=0.05).

absent_reason.analysis_set: Results refer to 89 randomized patients, but no source explicitly identifies ITT, mITT, per-protocol, or all randomized patients as the analysis set.
absent_reason.follow_up: No source states the outcome assessment timepoint or follow-up duration. Median hospitalization durations do not establish the endpoint follow-up.

served_mismatch: The reported effect and confidence interval are OR, whereas the served estimand is RR. The served row acknowledges this scale correction and quotes matching arm counts, but supplies no numeric corrected RR or RR confidence interval to verify. Its intention-to-treat label and study-end timepoint are not explicitly supported by the held sources.

candidate_rejections.why: The French abstract labels the same effect RR, conflicting with the English abstract's OR label. This cannot support using 0.34 and its interval as an RR; bind the English OR and the reported arm counts.

entry_population_matches_question.why: The entry population is described as hospitalized patients; antibiotic receipt as an entry criterion is not explicitly stated.
entry_population_matches_question.span: In this double-blind, randomized study, hospitalized patients were randomly assigned to receive either a lactobacilli-fermented milk or a placebo on a daily basis.

notes: The ft_ file contains abstracts and metadata, not the article body. BOUND applies to the reported OR and its CI; no RR or RR CI was inferred. Dose, detailed eligibility criteria, and an operational diarrhea definition are not stated.
